[0001] The present application claims the priority benefit of Republic of Korea Patent Application No. 10-2021-0191084 filed in Republic of Korea on December 29, 2021 , which is hereby incorporated by reference herein in its entirety.
BACKGROUND
Technical Field

[0002] The present disclosure relates to an organic light emitting diode display device, and more particularly, to an organic light emitting diode display device where a lateral leakage current and a rising of a low level voltage are prevented.
Discussion of the Related Art

[0003] Recently, with the advent of a multimedia an importance of a flat panel display has increased. Accordingly, a flat panel display such as a liquid crystal display device, a plasma display panel and an organic light emitting diode display device has been commercialized. Among the various flat panel displays, an organic light emitting diode (OLED) display device has been widely used due to a high response speed, a high luminance and a wide viewing angle.

[0004] However, in the OLED display device, since a lateral leakage current is generated and a low level voltage rises, a driving voltage and a power consumption increase and a uniformity of a luminance is deteriorated.
SUMMARY

[0005] Accordingly, the present disclosure is directed to an organic light emitting diode display device that substantially obviate one or more of the problems due to limitations and disadvantages of the related art.

[0006] An object of the present disclosure is to provide an organic light emitting display device where a lateral leakage current is minimized and a rising of a low level voltage is prevented. An invention is defined in the claims.

[0007] Additional features and advantages of the disclosure will be set forth in the description which follows, and in part will be apparent from the description, or may be learned by practice of the disclosure. These and other advantages of the disclosure will be realized and attained by the structure particularly pointed out in the written description and claims hereof as well as the appended drawings.

[0008] To achieve these and other advantages and in accordance with the purpose of the present disclosure, as embodied and broadly described herein, a display device includes: a first substrate; a bank layer on the first substrate to define red, green and blue subpixels; a thin film transistor in each of the red, green and blue subpixels; a light emitting diode in each of the red, green and blue subpixels; and a plurality of spacers in a periphery of the red subpixel on the bank layer, wherein the light emitting diode includes an anode, a hole transporting layer, an emitting layer, an electron transporting layer and a cathode, wherein each of the plurality of spacers has a reverse taper shape, wherein the hole transporting layer and the electron transporting layer extend to an adjacent subpixel through side and top surfaces of each of the plurality of spacers, and wherein the cathode is cut due to the side surface of each of the plurality of spacers. Herein, a reverse taper shape may mean a shape which tapers towards the first substrate. That is, a reverse taper shape may be a taper which is widest towards an upper surface of the display device, and narrowest towards the first substrate of the display device. Herein, the upper surface of the display device may be defined as a surface through which light is extracted from the display device. The upper surface may be defined by a second substrate herein.

[0009] It is to be understood that both the foregoing general description and the following detailed description are explanatory and are intended to provide further explanation of the disclosure as claimed.

[0017] Hereinafter, an organic light emitting diode display device according to embodiments of the present disclosure will be described in detail with reference to the accompanying drawings. In the following description, like reference numerals designate like elements throughout. When a detailed description of well-known functions or configurations related to this document is determined to unnecessarily cloud a gist of the inventive concept, the detailed description thereof will be omitted or will be made brief.
[0018] FIG. 1 is a view showing an organic light emitting diode display device according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure.

[0019] In FIG. 1 , an organic light emitting diode (OLED) display device 100 according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure includes an image processing unit 101, a timing controlling unit 102, a gate driving unit 103, a data driving unit 104, a power supplying unit 106 and a display panel PNL.

[0020] The image processing unit 101 outputs an image data and a plurality of timing signals for driving various units. For example, the plurality of timing signals outputted from the image processing unit 101 may include a data enable signal, a horizontal synchronization signal, a vertical synchronization signal and a clock signal.

[0021] The timing controlling unit 102 receives the image data and the plurality of timing signals from the image processing unit 101. The timing controlling unit 102 generates and outputs a gate control signal GDC for controlling an operation timing of the gate driving unit 103 and a data control signal DDC for controlling an operation timing of the data driving unit 104 based on the plurality of timing signals supplied from the image processing unit 101.

[0022] The gate driving unit 103 outputs a scan signal to the display panel PNL in response to the gate control signal supplied from the timing controlling unit 102. The gate driving unit 103 outputs the scan signal through a plurality of gate lines GL1 to GLm. Although the gate driving unit 103 may be formed as an integrated circuit (IC), it is not limited thereto. Specifically, the gate driving unit 103 may have a gate-in-panel (GIP) structure where a thin film transistor are formed on a substrate of the OLED display device 100. The GIP structure may include a plurality of circuits such as a shift register and a level shifter.

[0023] The data driving unit 104 outputs a data voltage to the display panel PNL in response to the data control signal DDC supplied from the timing controlling unit 102. The data driving unit 104 performs a sampling and a latch of a data signal DATA of a digital type supplied from the timing controlling unit 102 and coverts the data signal DATA into the data voltage of an analog type based on a gamma voltage. The data driving unit 104 outputs the data voltage through a plurality of data lines DL1 to DLn.

[0024] Although the data driving unit 104 may be mounted on the display panel PNL as an integrated circuit (IC) or may be laminated directly on the display panel PNL as various patterns and layers, it is not limited thereto.

[0025] The power supplying unit 106 outputs and supplies a high level voltage EVDD and a low level voltage EVSS to the display panel PNL. The high level voltage EVDD and the low level voltage EVSS are supplied to the display panel PNL through a power line. The voltages outputted from the power supplying unit 106 may be transmitted to the gate driving unit 104 or the data driving unit 104 for driving the gate driving unit 104 or the data driving unit 104.

[0026] The display panel PNL displays an image in response to the scan signal, the data voltage and the voltages supplied from the gate driving unit 103, the data driving unit 104 and the power supplying unit 106, respectively.

[0027] The display panel PNL includes a plurality of subpixels SP for displaying an image. The plurality of subpixels SP includes red, green and blue subpixels or white, red, green and blue subpixels. The white, red, green and blue subpixels may have the same area as each other or may have different areas from each other.
[0028] FIG. 2 is a circuit diagram showing a subpixel of a display panel PNL of an organic light emitting diode display device according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure.

[0029] The display panel PNL of the OLED display device 100 includes a display area and a pad area, and the display area includes the plurality of subpixels SP. Each subpixel SP displays a single color in the OLED display device 100. For example, each subpixel SP may display one of red, green, blue and white colors, and red, green, blue and white subpixels SP may be defined as a single pixel. The plurality of subpixels SP are disposed in a matrix on a substrate of the OLED display device 100, and a plurality of lines are disposed between the plurality of subpixels SP in the display area.

[0030] Further, a plurality of link lines electrically connected to the plurality of lines in the display area and supplying signals to elements of the OLED display device 100 may be disposed in the pad area. For example, the plurality of link lines may include a high level voltage (Vdd) line, a data voltage (Vdata) line, a reference voltage (Vref) line and a low level voltage (Vss) line.

[0031] In FIG. 2 , each subpixel SP of the display panel PNL of the OLED display device 100 includes a switching thin film transistor (TFT) T1, a driving TFT T2, a storage capacitor Cst, a sensing TFT T3, an auxiliary TFT T4 and a light emitting diode E. Since the subpixel SP of the OLED display device 100 includes 4 TFTs and 1 capacitor, the subpixel SP may be referred to as a 4T1C structure. However, a structure of the subpixel SP of the OLED display device 100 is not limited thereto. For example, the subpixel SP may have various structures such as a 4T2C structure including 4 TFTs and 2 capacitors, a 5T2C structure including 5 TFTs and 2 capacitors, a 6T2C structure including 6 TFTs and 2 capacitors and a 7T2C structure including 7 TFTs and 2 capacitors.

[0032] Each of 4 TFTs in the subpixel SP includes a semiconductor layer, a gate electrode, a source electrode and a drain electrode, and may have a positive type or a negative type. For convenience of illustration, FIG. 2 exemplarily shows a negative type thin film transistor.

[0033] The switching TFT T1 includes a drain electrode connected to the data line, a source electrode connected to a first node N1 and a gate electrode connected to the gate line. The switching TFT T1 is turned on according to the gate voltage Vg applied to the gate line from the gate driving unit and transmits the data voltage Vdata applied through the data line from the data driving unit to the first node N1.

[0034] The driving TFT T2 includes a drain electrode connected to a high level voltage (Vdd) line, a source electrode connected to an anode of the light emitting diode E and a gate electrode connected to the first node N1. The driving TFT T2 is turned on when a voltage of the first node N1 is greater than a threshold voltage Vth and is turned off when a voltage of the first node N1 is smaller than a threshold voltage Vth. The driving TFT T2 transmits a driving current of the high level voltage (Vdd) line to the light emitting diode E.

[0035] The storage capacitor Cst includes a first electrode connected to the first node N1 and a second node N2 connected to the source electrode of the driving TFT T2. The storage capacitor Cst keeps a voltage difference between the gate electrode and the source electrode of the driving TFT T2 constant during an emission time where the light emitting diode E emits a light so that a constant driving current can be transmitted to the light emitting diode E.

[0036] The sensing TFT T3 includes a drain electrode connected to the source electrode of the driving TFT T2, a source electrode connected to the reference line and a gate electrode connected to a sensing line. The sensing TFT T3 is a thin film transistor for sensing the threshold voltage of the driving TFT T2.

[0037] The auxiliary TFT T4 includes a drain electrode electrically connected to a cathode of the light emitting diode E, a source electrode electrically connected to the reference line and a gate electrode electrically connected to an auxiliary line. The auxiliary TFT T4 is turned on during an emission period to transmit the low level voltage Vss to the cathode of the light emitting diode E.
[0038] FIG. 3 is a plan view showing an organic light emitting diode display device according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure.

[0039] In FIG. 3 , the OLED display device 100 may include a red subpixel SP _R, a green subpixel SP_G and a blue subpixel SP_B. Although the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B have a specific shape and are disposed in a specific arrangement in FIG. 3 , the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B may have various shape and may be disposed in a various arrangement in another embodiment.

[0040] A plurality of spacers 154 each having a reversed taper shape in a cross-sectional view are disposed in a periphery of the red subpixel SP_R, while the plurality of spacers 154 are not disposed in a periphery of the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B. In each spacer 154 having a reversed taper shape, a width of a top portion (top surface) is greater than a width of the bottom portion (bottom surface).

[0041] The plurality of spacers 154 each having a bar shape in a plan view are disposed in four peripheral sides of the red subpixel SP_R to surround the red subpixel SP_R. The plurality of spacers 154 surrounding the red subpixel SP_R are spaced apart from each other. Although four spacers 154 are disposed in a rectangular shape and the red subpixel SP_R is disposed in the rectangular shape in FIG. 3 , the spacers 154 equal to or greater than five may be disposed in a polygonal shape or a circular shape and the red subpixel SP_R may be disposed in the polygonal shape or the circular shape in another embodiment.

[0042] Although each of the plurality of spacers 154 includes two of first and second sub-spacers 154a and 154b spaced apart from each other in FIG. 3 , it is not limited thereto. For example, each of the plurality of spacers 154 may include one sub-spacer or three sub-spacers in another embodiment. As a result, a plurality of first sub-spacers 154a and a plurality of second sub-spacers 154b may be disposed in a periphery of the red subpixel SP_R.

[0043] FIG. 4 is a cross-sectional view taken along a line IV-IV' of FIG. 3 , and FIG. 5 is a cross-sectional view taken along a line V-V' of FIG. 3 . FIG. 4 shows the red subpixel SP_R and the green subpixel SP_G adjacent to each other, and FIG. 5 shows the blue subpixel SP_B and the green subpixel SP_G adjacent to each other. FIG. 6 is a view showing current paths of a low level voltage of an organic light emitting diode display device according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure.

[0044] In FIGs. 4 and 5 , a thin film transistor (TFT) T is disposed in each of the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B. Although a plurality of TFTs such as the switching TFT, the driving TFT, the sensing TFT and the auxiliary TFT may be disposed in each of the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B, the one TFT T is shown for convenience of illustration. As a result, the one TFT T may be one of the switching TFT, the driving TFT, the sensing TFT and the auxiliary TFT.
[0045] Since the switching TFT, the driving TFT, the sensing TFT and the auxiliary TFT may have the same structure as each other, the one TFT T may represent the structure of the plurality of TFTs.

[0046] The TFT T includes a semiconductor layer 114 on a buffer layer 142 over a first substrate 110, a gate insulating layer 143 covering the semiconductor layer 114 on the buffer layer 142, a gate electrode 116 on the gate insulating layer 143, an interlayer insulating layer 144 covering the gate electrode 116 over the gate insulating layer 143 and source and drain electrodes 122 and 124 on the interlayer insulating layer 144.

[0047] The first substrate 110 may include a foldable plastic. For example, the first substrate 110 may include one of polyimide (PI), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene naphthalate (PEN), polycarbonate (PC), polyethersulfone (PES), polyarylate (PAR), polysulfone (PSF) and cyclic-olefin copolymer (COC). However, the first substrate 110 is not limited to the foldable material, and the first substrate 110 may include a hard material such as a glass.

[0048] The buffer layer 142 protects the TFT T from an impurity such as an alkali ion leaked from the first substrate 110 or blocks a moisture injected from an exterior. The buffer layer 142 may have a single layer or a multiple layer of silicon oxide (SiOx) or silicon nitride (SiNx).

[0049] The semiconductor layer 114 may include an amorphous semiconductor material such as amorphous silicon (a-Si), a polycrystalline semiconductor material such as polycrystalline silicon (p-Si) and an oxide semiconductor material such as indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO). The semiconductor layer 114 includes a channel region 114a of a central portion and source and drain regions 114b and 114c of a doped impurity at both sides of the channel region 114a.

[0050] Although the gate electrode 116 may have a single layer or a multiple layer of a metallic material such as chromium (Cr), molybdenum (Mo), tantalum (Ta), copper (Cu), titanium (Ti), aluminum (Al) or aluminum alloy, it is not limited thereto.

[0051] The interlayer insulating layer 144 may include an organic material such as photoacryl or may have a single layer or a multiple layer of an inorganic material such as silicon nitride (SiNx) or silicon oxide (SiOx). In addition, the interlayer insulating layer 144 may have a multiple layer of an organic layer and an inorganic layer.

[0052] Source and drain electrodes 122 and 124 are connected to the source and drain regions 114b and 114c, respectively, of the semiconductor layer 114 through first and second contact holes 149a and 149b in the gate insulating layer 143 and the interlayer insulating layer 144.

[0053] Although not shown, a bottom shield metal layer may be disposed under the semiconductor layer 114 on the first substrate 110. The bottom shield metal layer prevents deterioration of the TFT T and a residual image by minimizing a back channel phenomenon due to charges trapped in the first substrate 110. Although the bottom shield metal layer may have a single layer or a multiple layer of an alloy of titanium (Ti), molybdenum (Mo) or an alloy thereof, it is not limited thereto.

[0054] A passivation layer 146 is disposed on the TFT T and the entire first substrate 110. The passivation layer 146 may include an organic material such as photoacryl. Alternatively, the passivation layer 146 may have a multiple layer of an inorganic layer and an organic layer. The passivation layer 146 has a third contact hole 249c exposing the drain electrode 124.

[0055] An anode 132 electrically connected to the drain electrode 124 of the TFT T through the third contact hole 149c is disposed on the passivation layer 146 in each of the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B. The anode 132 may have a single layer or a multiple layer of a metallic material such as calcium (Ca), barium (Ba), magnesium (Mg), aluminum (Al) and silver (Ag) or an alloy thereof. The anode 132 is connected to the drain electrode 124 of the TFT T and an image signal is applied to the anode 132.

[0056] A bank layer 152 is disposed in a boundary region of each of the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B. The bank layer 152 may be a sidewall defining each of the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B and may prevent a mixture of colored lights emitted from the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B by dividing the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B.

[0057] The reversely tapered spacer 154 is disposed on the bank layer 152 in a periphery of the red subpixel SP_R. Although the spacer 154 includes the first and second sub-spacers 154a and 154b spaced apart from each other in FIG. 4 , the spacer 154 may include one sub-spacer or three or more sub-spacers in another embodiment. As shown in FIG. 5 , the spacer 154 is not disposed in a region not adjacent to the red subpixel SP_R (e.g., a region between the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B).

[0058] Although the bank layer 152 may include polyimide (PI) or photoresist, it is not limited thereto. The spacer 154 may have the same material as the bank layer 152 or may have a different material from the bank layer 152. For example, when the spacer 154 and the bank layer 152 include the same material as each other, the spacer 154 and the bank layer 152 may be formed through a single mask process.

[0059] A hole transporting layer 134 is disposed on the anode 132 between the adjacent bank layers 152, an top surface of the bank layer 152 and side and top surfaces of the spacer 154, and an emitting layer 135 is disposed on the hole transporting layer 134 between the adjacent bank layers 152. The emitting layer 135 may include a red emitting layer emitting a red colored light in the red subpixel SP_R, a green emitting layer emitting a green colored light in the green subpixel SP_G and a blue emitting layer emitting a blue colored light in the blue subpixel SP_B. Alternatively, the emitting layer 135 may include a white emitting layer emitting a white colored light in the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B.

[0060] An electron transporting layer 136 is disposed on the emitting layer 135 between the adjacent bank layer 152, the hole transporting layer 134 over the top surface of the bank layer 152 and the hole transporting layer 134 over the side and top surfaces of the spacer 154.

[0061] A cathode 138 is disposed on the electron transporting layer 136 between the adjacent bank layers 152, the electron transporting layer 136 over the top surface of the bank layer 152 and the electron transporting layer 136 over the top surface of the spacer 154. The cathode 138 is not disposed on the electron transporting layer 136 over the side surface of the spacer 154. Although the cathode 138 is disposed over the top surface of the bank layer 152 and the top surface of the spacer 154, the cathode 138 is not disposed over the side surface of the reversely tapered spacer 154. As a result, the cathode 138 over the top surface of the bank layer 152 and the cathode 138 over the top surface of the spacer 154 are cut due to the side surface of the reversely tapered spacer 154.

[0062] Although not shown, a hole injecting layer may be disposed between the anode 132 and the hole transporting layer 134, and an electron injecting layer may be disposed on the electron transporting layer 136.

[0063] The anode 132, the hole transporting layer 134, the emitting layer 135, the electron transporting layer 136 and the cathode 138 constitute the light emitting diode E emitting a light of a predetermined wavelength according to a signal applied from an exterior.

[0064] In the OLED display device 100 according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure, since the hole transporting layer 134 and the electron transporting layer 136 are disposed on the side and top surfaces of the spacer 154, the hole transporting layer 134 and the electron transporting layer 136 are disposed on an entire surface of the OLED display device 100. The cathode 138 is cut due to the spacer 154.
[0065] As a result, a current path through the hole transporting layer 134 is elongated, and a lateral leakage current is reduced.

[0066] When the subpixel is driven to have an on state in the OLED display device 100, a lateral leakage current is generated and is transmitted to the adjacent subpixel. Since the lateral leakage current causes an error in a current of the adjacent subpixel, a uniformity of a luminance between the subpixels is deteriorated. In addition, the adjacent subpixel having an off state may be turned on due to the lateral leakage current to emit a light. Specifically, since a gap distance between the subpixels is reduced in a high resolution display device, a bad influence of the lateral leakage current increases.

[0067] The lateral leakage current flows through a common layer such as the hole transporting layer 134, the electron transporting layer 136, the hole injecting layer and the electron injecting layer to be transmitted to the adjacent subpixel. In the OLED display device 100, a transmission of the lateral leakage current to the adjacent subpixel is minimized by adjusting a current path of the lateral leakage current.

[0068] Since the hole transporting layer 134 and the electron transporting layer 136 are disposed on the side and top surfaces of the spacer 154, the current path of the lateral leakage current is elongated. As a result, the lateral leakage current transmitted to the adjacent subpixel is minimized due to an increase of a length of the current path.

[0069] The cathode 138 is formed of a transparent conductive material such as indium tin oxide (ITO) and indium zinc oxide (IZO) or a metallic material of a thin thickness which a visible ray passes through. As a result, the transparent conductive material or the metallic material is not formed on the side surface of the reversely tapered spacer 154 during a forming process for the cathode 138 such as a sputtering process.

[0070] Accordingly, the cathode 138 over a whole of the OLED display device 100 is cut in a region of the spacer 154, and an increase of a length of a current path of the low level voltage Vss is prevented. The current of the low level voltage Vss flows through the cathode 138. The increase of the length of the current path of the low level voltage Vss causes a rising of the low level voltage Vss. A driving voltage and a power consumption increase and a uniformity of a luminance is deteriorated due to the rising of the low level voltage Vss.

[0071] When the cathode 138 is not cut by the spacer 154, the cathode 154 extends to the side and top surfaces of the spacer 154. As a result, the current path of the low level voltage Vss is elongated and the low level voltage Vss increases.

[0072] In the OLED display device 100, the cathode 138 is cut in the region of the reversely tapered spacer 154 to prevent the rising of the low level voltage Vss. Since the current path of the low level voltage Vss is prevented from being formed on the top and side surfaces of the first spacer 154a and the top and side surfaces of the second spacer 154b, the increase of the current path of the low level voltage Vss is minimized due to the spacer 154.

[0073] In the OLED display device 100 according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure, the spacer 154 having a reverse taper shape is disposed on the bank layer 152. As a result, the current path of the lateral leakage current is elongated and the lateral leakage current to the adjacent subpixel is minimized. Further, the increase of the length of the current path of the low level voltage Vss is minimized and the rising of the low level voltage Vss is minimized.

[0074] In the OLED display device 100 according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure, the spacer 154 is disposed in a periphery of the red subpixel SP_R and is not disposed in a periphery of the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B.

[0075] When the reversely tapered spacer 154 is disposed on the bank layer 152, the cathode 138 is cut in the region of the spacer 154. However, the current path is elongated as compared with a comparison example where the spacer 154 is omitted.

[0076] In FIG. 6 , since a first current path of the low level voltage Vss passing through the spacer 154 is cut due to the reversely tapered spacer 154, the current of the low level voltage Vss is not transmitted to the red subpixel SP_R through the first current path of the low level voltage Vss. Instead, the current of the low level voltage Vss is transmitted to the red subpixel SP_R through a second current path of the low level voltage Vss outside the spacer 154. Since a length of the current path of the low level voltage Vss increases as compared with a comparison example where the spacer 154 is omitted and the current of the low level voltage Vss is transmitted through the first current path, a property of the OLED display device 100 may be deteriorated due to the rising of the low level voltage.

[0077] As a result, when the reversely tapered spacer 154 is disposed on the bank layer 152, the OLED device 100 has an advantage that the lateral leakage current decreases and a disadvantage that the low level voltage increases.

[0078] In the OLED display device 100 according to a first embodiment of the present disclosure, the advantage the lateral leakage current decreases is maximized and the disadvantage that that the low level voltage increases is minimized. As a result, an efficiency of the OLED display device 100 is improved.

[0079] Among the red, green and blue subpixels SP_R, SP_G and SP_B, a relatively small current is applied to the red subpixel SP_R and a relatively great current is applied to the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B. The TFT T in the red subpixel SP_R has a relatively low threshold voltage and the TFT T in the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B has a relatively high threshold voltage.

[0080] As a result, in the red subpixel SP_R, the current may have a relatively great variation and the luminance may have a relatively great change even when a relatively small lateral leakage current is applied. In addition, the red subpixel SP_R having an off state may emit a light due to a relatively small lateral leakage current. In the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B, the current may have a relatively small variation and the luminance may have a relatively small change when a relatively small lateral leakage current is applied. In addition, the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B having an off state may not emit a light due to a relatively small lateral leakage current. The red subpixel SP_R has a relatively great influence by the lateral leakage current, while the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B have a relatively small influence by the lateral leakage current.
[0081] Accordingly, in the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B, deterioration due to the lateral leakage current may not occur even when the spacer 154 is not disposed in the periphery.

[0082] In the OLED display device 100, the spacer 154 is disposed in the periphery of the red subpixel SP_R having a maximum influence by the lateral leakage current, and the spacer 154 is not disposed in the periphery of the green and blue subpixels SP_G and SP_B having a minimum influence by the lateral leakage current. As a result, deterioration due to the lateral leakage current is prevented.
[0083] Further, since the spacer 154 is disposed in a minimal region (a periphery of the red subpixel SP_R), the rising of the low level voltage Vss due to the spacer 154 is minimized.

[0084] In FIGs. 4 and 5 , an encapsulation layer 160 is disposed on the cathode 136. The encapsulation layer 160 may include a first encapsulation layer 162 of an inorganic material, a second encapsulation layer 164 of an organic material and a third encapsulation layer 166 of an inorganic material. Although the inorganic material may include silicon nitride (SiNx) and silicon oxide (SiOx), it is not limited thereto. Although the organic material may include polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene naphthalate (PEN), polycarbonate (PC), polyimide (PI), polyethylene sulfonate (PES), polyoxymethylene (POM), polyarylate (PAR) and a mixture thereof, it is not limited thereto.
